the generalization of large deep learning networks is still a mystery.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that deep neural networks generalize so well because they have a large capacity to represent functions that are smooth, have low complexity and have low variance.

the authors of [1] have shown that for a certain type of neural networks the generalization gap (the gap between training error and test error) can become arbitrarily small even if the network is over-parameterized (has more parameters than training data points).

the current state of the art is not able to account for the generalization capabilities of deep networks.
the generalization of large neural networks is indeed a mystery, and that we should not expect to find a simple explanation for it.
